mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the past three months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following RSAFS increases, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past two months signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) both increase by more than 5% over the past two months, it signals robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS increases on subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized, it signals tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of economic expansion, a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the past month signals strengthening labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances during economic expansions despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during expansions.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle economic phase, an increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past two months signals robust supply-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances during late-cycle expansions despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during late-cycle expansions.
